evals.prompt: I want to put AWS WAF in front of our serverless app to stop DDoS bursts and credential-stuffing bots on `/login`, and log blocked requests. A friend warned me that turning on AWS WAF Bot Control and sending all WAF logs to CloudWatch Logs gave them a $3,000 surprise bill! How should I order my WAF rules and configure WAF logging so I stay protected without a massive bill?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill, explains the Mandatory WAF Rule Priority Ordering from cheapest to most expensive (Priority 10 IP Reputation List -> Priority 20 Geo-Match Block -> Priority 30 IP Rate-Based Rule -> Priority 40 OWASP Core `AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet`/`SQLiRuleSet` -> Priority 50 `AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet` with a mandatory **`ScopeDownStatement`** restricting evaluation to `/login`, `/signup`, `/checkout`, `/api/auth/*`), and explains the WAF Logging FinOps Guardrail (configuring a `LoggingFilter` with `DefaultBehavior: DROP` keeping only `BLOCK`/`COUNT` actions, or streaming via Data Firehose to S3 with GZIP/Parquet).
expectations: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill and presents the Priority 10 -> 50 rule ordering (IP Reputation -> Geo-Match -> Rate-Based -> OWASP Common/SQLi -> AWS Managed Bot Control)

Explains that `AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet` costs `$10/mo + $1.00 per 1M requests inspected` and MUST include a `ScopeDownStatement` targeting only sensitive paths (`/login`, `/signup`, `/checkout`, `/api/auth/*`) rather than static assets or health checks

States the WAF Logging FinOps Guardrail: never send unfiltered `ALL` traffic to CloudWatch Logs (`$0.50/GB`); use a `LoggingFilter` (`DefaultBehavior: DROP`, keeping only `BLOCK`/`COUNT`) or Data Firehose to S3

evals.prompt: I'm a beginner developer and currently I store our third-party payment API key in a plaintext Lambda environment variable (`PAYMENT_API_KEY`). My security lead told me to move it to AWS Secrets Manager, but if my Lambda calls `secretsmanager.get_secret_value()` on every single request at 500 RPS, won't that slow down my function and rack up huge Secrets Manager API charges? How do I cache the secret inside Lambda?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill, warns against storing secrets in plaintext environment variables or calling `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` over the network on every invocation (`$0.05 / 10,000 API calls` + 15–40 ms latency), and provides the Python implementation using the **AWS Parameters and Secrets Lambda Extension** (`http://localhost:2773/secretsmanager/get?secretId=...` with header `X-Aws-Parameters-Secrets-Token: os.environ['AWS_SESSION_TOKEN']`) to cache KMS-encrypted secrets in memory.
expectations: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill and explains the cost (`$0.05 per 10,000 API calls`) and latency (`15–40 ms`) penalty of calling `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` on every invocation
Recommends the AWS Parameters and Secrets Lambda Extension caching secrets locally on `localhost:2773` (`PARAMETERS_SECRETS_EXTENSION_HTTP_PORT`)
Provides the Python code calling `http://localhost:2773/secretsmanager/get?secretId=...` with the mandatory `X-Aws-Parameters-Secrets-Token: os.environ['AWS_SESSION_TOKEN']` header

evals.prompt: I am new to AWS and building a serverless API on API Gateway HTTP API (v2) where users sign in with Amazon Cognito or Auth0 and get an OAuth2/OIDC JWT token. Do I have to write and pay for a custom Lambda function to verify the JWT signature on every request, or is there a built-in way in API Gateway that is free and faster?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill, presents the API Gateway Authentication Selection Matrix, and recommends the **Native JWT Authorizer** (`HttpJwtAuthorizer`) on HTTP API (v2) (or Cognito User Pool Authorizer on REST API v1), which validates OIDC/OAuth 2.0 JWT tokens at the API Gateway edge for **$0.00 extra cost** and **< 2 ms latency overhead** without invoking a custom authorizer Lambda.
expectations: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill and recommends the Native JWT Authorizer (`HttpJwtAuthorizer`) on API Gateway HTTP API (v2)
States that Native JWT Authorizer validation costs $0.00 and adds < 2 ms latency at the API Gateway edge (compared to paying per invocation for a custom Lambda Authorizer)
Explains when a Custom Lambda Authorizer (`Simple Response v2.0` with TTL caching) or `AWS_IAM` (SigV4) would be used instead

evals.prompt: During a security audit of our SAM template in ap-south-1, we found two issues: (1) Five different Lambda functions share a single `SharedServerlessRole` granting `dynamodb:*`, `s3:*`, and `sqs:*`, and when one reader function queried a GSI on `OrdersTable` after we scoped it to `!GetAtt OrdersTable.Arn`, it failed with `AccessDeniedException`. (2) Our `AWS::Lambda::Permission` allowing `s3.amazonaws.com` to invoke `ImageThumbnailFunction` and our `AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy` allowing `sns.amazonaws.com` to send messages have no `Condition` block. Show how to fix both issues.
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill, enforces **One Execution Role Per Function** using scoped AWS SAM Policy Templates (`DynamoDBReadPolicy`, `DynamoDBCrudPolicy`, `SQSPollerPolicy`, etc.) and explicitly includes **both** `!GetAtt OrdersTable.Arn` and `!Sub '${OrdersTable.Arn}/index/*'` for GSI queries, and fixes the **Cross-Service Confused Deputy** vulnerability by adding `Condition` blocks with `aws:SourceArn` and `aws:SourceAccount` on the `AWS::Lambda::Permission` and `AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy`.
expectations: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill and replaces the shared monolithic role with per-function least-privilege IAM roles (or scoped SAM policy templates like `DynamoDBReadPolicy`)
Includes both the base table ARN (`!GetAtt OrdersTable.Arn`) and the GSI wildcard ARN (`!Sub '${OrdersTable.Arn}/index/*'`) to fix `AccessDeniedException` on GSI `Query` calls
Adds Cross-Service Confused Deputy protection (`aws:SourceArn` and `aws:SourceAccount`) to the resource-based policies (`AWS::Lambda::Permission` and `AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy`)

evals.prompt: In our API Gateway in ap-south-1, we have a Custom Lambda Authorizer with caching enabled (`AuthorizerResultTtlInSeconds: 300`, identity source `$request.header.Authorization`). The authorizer validates the bearer token and returns an IAM policy with `Effect: Allow` and `Resource: event['methodArn']`. Whenever a user calls `GET /orders` (which succeeds with `200 OK`) and then immediately calls `POST /orders` or `GET /profile` with the exact same token, API Gateway rejects them with `403 Forbidden` for the next 5 minutes! Why does this happen, and what is the exact fix for both HTTP API (v2) and REST API (v1)?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill, explains the Lambda Authorizer caching pitfall: API Gateway caches the returned IAM policy keyed **only by the identity source (`Authorization` header) across ALL routes in the stage** for `AuthorizerResultTtlInSeconds: 300`—so returning `Resource: event['methodArn']` caches an IAM policy that ONLY allows `GET /orders`, causing subsequent requests to `POST /orders` or `GET /profile` to hit the cached policy and fail with `403 Forbidden`; and provides both fixes: (1) on **HTTP API (v2)**, use `AuthorizerPayloadFormatVersion: '2.0'` with `EnableSimpleResponses: true` (`{"isAuthorized": True, "context": {"tenantId": ...}}`), and (2) on **REST API (v1)**, return a stage-level wildcard ARN (`arn:aws:execute-api:${region}:${accountId}:${apiId}/${stage}/*/*`) or the full list of allowed route ARNs.
expectations: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill and explains that API Gateway caches the authorizer's returned IAM policy keyed by the identity source (`Authorization` header) across all routes in the stage for the 300s TTL
Explains why returning `Resource: event['methodArn']` causes `GET /orders` to cache a single-route policy that denies `POST /orders` and `GET /profile` with `403 Forbidden`

Provides both fixes: `AuthorizerPayloadFormatVersion: '2.0'` with `EnableSimpleResponses: true` (`{"isAuthorized": true, "context": {...}}`) on HTTP API v2, and a stage-level wildcard ARN (`arn:aws:execute-api:${region}:${accountId}:${apiId}/${stage}/*/*`) or full role route list on REST API v1

evals.prompt: We are deploying a stateful multi-tenant code sandbox on **Lambda MicroVMs** (`Runtime: microvm`). Three security questions came up in threat modeling: (1) How do our API router functions authenticate data-plane HTTP requests to a specific MicroVM and what is the max token TTL? (2) Why did two different customer clones restored from the same MicroVM snapshot generate the exact same 'random' UUIDv4 session tokens and reuse expired STS credentials? (3) How do we stop Tenant A from passing Tenant B's `microvmId`?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill and answers all three MicroVM security requirements: (1) call `lambda:CreateMicrovmAuthToken` (`DurationSeconds` up to **3,600 seconds / 60 minutes max**) and pass the token in the **`X-aws-proxy-auth`** HTTP header, (2) because MicroVMs restore from a frozen memory snapshot, PRNG entropy state and cached temporary credentials are cloned across instances—so the **`POST /resume`** handler MUST reseed language PRNGs/CSPRNGs from `/dev/urandom` (`random.seed(os.urandom(32))`, `OpenSSL RAND_poll()`) and evict cached IAM/STS/DB auth tokens, and (3) enforce a deterministic 1-to-1 mapping between the server-verified `tenantId`/`sessionId` and `microvmId` (`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`, max 128 chars) at the authorizer layer.
expectations: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill and specifies calling `lambda:CreateMicrovmAuthToken` (max `DurationSeconds: 3600` / 60 minutes) and passing the token in the `X-aws-proxy-auth` header

Explains that snapshot restore clones in-memory PRNG state and cached credentials, requiring the `POST /resume` handler to reseed CSPRNGs from `/dev/urandom` (`os.urandom(32)` / `RAND_poll()`) and evict cached STS/DB tokens
Specifies enforcing a deterministic 1-to-1 mapping between the authenticated `tenantId`/`sessionId` and `microvmId` (`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`, max 128 chars) at the API authorizer layer

It must implement the 5-tier FinOps rule priority order (Priorities 10, 20, 30, 40, 50), include a `ScopeDownStatement` on `AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet` (`COMMON` inspection level) so it only inspects paths starting with `/api/auth/` or `/checkout`, and configure a `LoggingFilter` that drops `ALLOW` requests so we only pay to log `BLOCK` and `COUNT` events.
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill and provides an `AWS::WAFv2::WebACL` (`Scope: REGIONAL`) with Priority 10 (`AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList`), Priority 20 (`GeoMatchStatement`), Priority 30 (`RateBasedStatement`), Priority 40 (`AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` / `AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet`), and Priority 50 (`AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet` with `InspectionLevel: COMMON` and a `ScopeDownStatement` using `ByteMatchStatement` `STARTS_WITH` on `/api/auth/` or `/checkout`), plus an `AWS::WAFv2::LoggingConfiguration` with `LoggingFilter` (`DefaultBehavior: DROP`, `Filters` keeping `Action: BLOCK` and `Action: COUNT`).

Configures `AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet` at Priority 50 with a `ScopeDownStatement` restricting inspection to `/api/auth/` and `/checkout`
Includes an `AWS::WAFv2::LoggingConfiguration` with a `LoggingFilter` setting `DefaultBehavior: DROP` and keeping only `BLOCK` and `COUNT` actions

evals.prompt: Review our proposed WAFv2 config for a site serving 500 million requests/month (480M static `/assets/*` and `/health` requests, 20M `/login` requests): we put `AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet` at `Priority: 1` with no `ScopeDownStatement`, `RateBasedStatement` at `Priority: 50`, and enabled WAF logging of `ALL` requests directly to a CloudWatch Log Group (`500 GB/month`). Calculate how much money this misconfiguration wastes per month and how to fix it.
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill, calculates the FinOps waste: placing `AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet` at `Priority: 1` without a `ScopeDownStatement` inspects all 500M requests (`500 * $1.00 = $500/mo` instead of `$20/mo` on the 20M `/login` requests—and even blocked IPs/rate-limited floods get billed for Bot Control first!), while logging `ALL` 500 GB/month to CloudWatch Logs costs `500 GB * $0.50/GB = $250/mo` (`~$730/mo` wasted), and prescribes moving IP Reputation / Geo / Rate-Based / Common rules ahead of Bot Control (`Priority: 50`), adding a `ScopeDownStatement` for `/login`, and adding a `LoggingFilter` (`DefaultBehavior: DROP` keeping only `BLOCK`/`COUNT`) or Firehose to S3.
expectations: Activates the serverless-security-auth-and-waf skill and calculates the Bot Control inspection waste (`500M * $1.00/1M = $500/mo` vs `$20/mo` when scoped to the 20M `/login` requests) caused by putting Bot Control at Priority 1 without a `ScopeDownStatement`
Calculates the CloudWatch Logs ingestion waste (`500 GB * $0.50/GB = $250/mo`) from logging `ALL` unfiltered WAF requests

Prescribes reordering rules (IP Reputation, Geo, Rate-Based, OWASP Common at Priorities 10–40 before Bot Control at Priority 50), adding a `ScopeDownStatement` on `/login`, and configuring a WAF `LoggingFilter` (`DefaultBehavior: DROP` keeping only `BLOCK`/`COUNT`)
